I'm stopping before any fix dispatch, because the only fix the review accepts conflicts with the plan.

The review says the fix is changing `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py` line 88. The plan's Global Constraints say "Do not edit anything under `vendor/`; a script syncs it from upstream." Whether the finding or the constraint governs is your decision, so I'm making no edits and dispatching no fix subagent. No fix attempt is spent, and Task 4 stays unmarked in the ledger.

The one thing I'd do first is a read-only look at the line, so I can quote it exactly:

<command>
sed -n 80,95p vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py
</command>

Message to my partner:

> Task 4 (`runs_on`, commit 7c1d9e0) failed review on a problem in vendored code, and I need your call before I fix anything.
>
> **Finding:** `runs_on` returns True on 2026-12-25, which has a removal exception, so the Step 1 test fails against a real feed. `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py` line 88 compares `exception_type` to the string `'1'`, but the parser yields the integer `1`. Every removal is therefore read as an addition. The parsed objects are frozen, so nothing outside `vendor/` can correct the value. The reviewer found the rest of the task matches the brief.
>
> **Conflict:** the plan's Global Constraints say not to edit anything under `vendor/`, because a script syncs it from upstream. The only fix the review identifies is a one-line change there.
>
> **Options:**
> 1. **Fix upstream, then re-sync (recommended).** The change survives the next sync and the constraint stays intact. Task 4 stays blocked until the upstream fix lands.
> 2. **Patch `vendor/` locally.** I'd dispatch a fix subagent for the one-line change. The next sync will overwrite it unless the patch is also carried upstream or re-applied after each sync. This waives the constraint for this one line.
> 3. **Bypass the vendored parser for exceptions.** `ferry/exceptions.py` would read the exception rows itself. That avoids editing `vendor/`, but it departs from Step 2's "using the parsed calendar from `vendor/gtfs_lite`" and needs a plan amendment.
>
> Which governs? Once you choose, I'll dispatch the fix subagent for round 1 with `tests/test_exceptions.py` as the covering test, then run the scoped re-review.
